gaps: Every breath-one item is a price somebody pays, and the question asked what the payment does. Sharpening Six-minute increment produced a meter that teaches by a charge nobody incurs (the cancellation fee that keeps the client from cancelling), and setting that against the restaurant deposit produced a family of prices whose success is that they are never collected. This became breath two's question: what does a price do by not being paid, and what happens when it starts to be.
accepted: Velvet rope: a price set high enough that the crowd it admits becomes the product for everyone in it, as the nine-dollar coffee keeps the coworking floor quiet by pricing out anyone who came to sit for an afternoon, and the private bank's minimum balance sells its other clients' company; the carrier is the buyer population, the seller wants fewer buyers of a particular sort, and the quantity a clearing price would sell is the failure rather than the goal.

Price as testimony: where quality cannot be shown before purchase, a high price is the one claim a low-quality seller could not afford to keep making, as the consultant with no credential charges what the credentialed charge and the unknown wine sells at the price of the known; the carrier is the buyer's inference, it works only where repeat purchase exists since a one-shot fraud can charge anything once, and the clearing story reads demand rising with the price as an error. Contested: signaling, status display, and placebo-quality effects are hard to separate in the observed cases.

Go-away price: a bid padded past any number the seller expects to win, so an unwanted counterparty is refused without a refusal and the door stays open for the next job, as the roofer who dislikes the client quotes triple and the fisherman names a price for the tourist's charter he hopes never to run; unlike the rope, which thins a population in advance, this refuses one counterparty after seeing them, and it forks on acceptance, since a go-away price that is paid becomes an obligation at a number that was meant as compensation for reluctance.

Tier that makes the kind: a price band constitutes a category that did not exist before the number, so goods are compared only within the band and judged by the band's standards, as the third-class carriage made a class of passenger out of a fare, and a two-thousand-dollar bicycle is reviewed by different magazines than a two-hundred-dollar one from the same factory; the carrier is the catalog or the shelf, the price sits upstream of the good's identity rather than downstream of its quality, and unlike testimony it makes no claim, it makes a room.

Price for the stranger's eyes: a price set for a reader who is not party to the trade, because each recorded price is evidence in the next one, as the gallery bids on its own artist at auction so the record will not print a low number, the recorded house sale sets the neighbor's assessment, and the transfer price between two subsidiaries is addressed to the tax authority alone; the carrier is the public record, and the clearing story cannot explain a seller who refuses cash to protect a number. Exchange-ontologies lists Precedent as a good that can be traded; this is the mechanism by which an ordinary price takes a second job as precedent whether the parties want it or not.

Six-minute increment: the shape of a price teaches the buyer what the thing is for, as the lawyer's tenth-of-an-hour billing teaches the client not to call, the cloud's outbound-data fee teaches the customer that data stays put, and the free tier with a rate limit teaches the developer that this is a toy; the carrier is the meter, the instruction rides on the unit and the step rather than the number, and the clearing story treats the buyer's use as given when the price wrote it.

Fixed price, thin walls: the shape of a price decides which of the seller's own temptations is live, as the fixed-price build tempts the builder to thin the walls, time-and-materials tempts them to slow down, and capitation tempts the clinic to prefer the healthy; the carrier is the seller's margin at the margin, it mirrors the six-minute increment since here the meter instructs the seller, and the clearing story holds the seller's effort constant while the price is varying it.

Price that names the wrong payer: a price at one point set to hide a payment somewhere else, so the buyer cannot see whose interest the seller serves, as the free checking account paid by overdraft fees, the free search paid by the advertiser who is the actual customer, and the prison phone call priced high so that the price pays the jailer a commission; the carrier is the bundle or the tie, and the clearing story reads each price alone when the pair is the instrument.

Price that goes to sleep: a price chosen once and then paid by inertia, so its work is done at the moment of first acceptance and never again, as the subscription that renews and the default tip the screen suggests; the carrier is the auto-renewal, the seller optimizes the first sight rather than the recurring value, and the market never clears again after the first purchase. Leverage-discoveries lists the default as a lever; this is the price's own mechanism, which is to stop being seen.

Mates' rates: a price below market whose number is a statement of relation, which the buyer must not haggle over and must repay in kind, as the plumber's rate to a friend, the wholesale price extended to a cousin, and the guest-friend's token payment that says this is not a purchase; the carrier is the discount read as speech, it reverses the invoice since here a price keeps a trade inside a relation rather than ending one, and the clearing story sees a seller leaving money on the table.

Invoice that ends the favor: attaching a price to something that was given moves it out of the gift register, where obligation and shame keep it flowing, into the market register, where it is merely for sale, and the move does not reverse when the price is removed, as the daycare that fined late parents saw lateness rise, because a fine is a price for an option that shame had kept closed, and lateness stayed high after the fine was dropped; the carrier is the invoice, the price works by changing the kind of relation rather than the quantity traded, and the clearing story predicts the opposite sign. The one-way move rests on a small number of field studies and is contested; the mechanism is kept with that modality.

Peppercorn: the existence of any price at all, however small, moves a transfer into the register that courts and tax offices can see, as the peppercorn rent makes a lease enforceable and the one-dollar sale makes a gift into a purchase with a date and a buyer; the carrier is the contract, the magnitude is irrelevant, and the clearing story has no place for a price whose entire work is done by being nonzero.

residue.item: Penny turnstile: a trivial price charged so that every use becomes a recorded transaction and the seller can count demand it could never see when the good was free.
residue.why: Rejected: the price is not the carrier; a registration wall produces the same record with no number at all, and the part a price adds (a screen on intent) is carried by Deposit that comes back in breath two.

residue.item: Price that pays for silence: a settlement with a non-disclosure clause, a license fee to a patent holder who would otherwise sue, tribute to a protector; the good delivered is an absence that can never be checked against delivery.
residue.why: Rejected: decomposes into exchange-ontologies' Discretion and Protection as the goods plus an enforcement clause, and the enforcement half is Fee that holds the door; nothing the price itself does is left over.

residue.item: Anchor that never sells: the ten-thousand-dollar handbag in the window that makes the two-thousand-dollar one reasonable.
residue.why: Merged into Decoy that must not sell: an anchor is a decoy read from the neighbor's side, and first-mover-forecloses already carries anchoring a price expectation as a move; the decoy item keeps the part that is new, a price whose success is being declined.

residue.item: Congestion charge: a price that makes the driver pay the delay imposed on others.
residue.why: Rejected: clearing with an externality folded into the number; the price does exactly its ordinary job on a corrected cost, and the boundary claim now excludes this class.

residue.item: Scorched-earth price: a price cut so deep it warns entrants off.
residue.why: Rejected: first-mover-forecloses carries it (signal the scorched-earth pricing policy); as a price it is a threat about future prices, and the threat mechanism is kept in Fee that holds the door where the threat is the price itself.

residue.item: Early bird: a lower earlier price that buys a forecast and cash before the good exists.
residue.why: Rejected: clearing across time with the seller as buyer of information; the discount is a price paid for commitment and the number does its ordinary work for the other side. Left outside by the boundary claim on clearing with the date moved.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, one carrier and one miss per item
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real price usually does several of these at once.
The daycare fine and the signaling cases are contested field results and are carried with that modality in the item text.
Prices that clear across time or segments are deliberately outside.

gaps: The changed question yielded prices that are returned (Deposit that comes back), never collected (Fee that holds the door), attached to a good priced not to sell (Decoy that must not sell), listed but paid by no one (Rack rate), and, from the same non-payment family read backwards, a price built so no comparison can be made at all (Quote that cannot be compared). The territory pointer 'what a price does' stands and the slug is kept, but the of-sentence now includes prices that work by bare existence and by never being paid, and the live question sharpened from 'what breaks under optimization' to a loop: a door fee optimized as revenue becomes the open price of an option, the restraint does not return, and the seller must build a new door.
accepted: Deposit that comes back: a price returned if the buyer does what they said, so it rations requests by putting money at risk rather than by collecting it, as the restaurant deposit refunded on arrival, earnest money on a house, and bail; the carrier is escrow, the net price is zero for everyone who keeps their word, and the clearing story cannot see a price that changes hands twice and ends where it began. It also earns the seller float, which is the one number in it a spreadsheet will find.

Fee that holds the door: a price the seller hopes never to collect, as the cancellation fee, the late fee, and the liquidated-damages clause, which work by being believed and stop working when they are paid often, since a fee collected often enough to be optimized as revenue becomes a rack rate for lateness and the door it held swings open; the carrier is the threat, nothing changes hands on the good path where the deposit changes hands twice, and the clearing story sees a fee that is never paid as a price with no demand.

Decoy that must not sell: an item priced so that its neighbor looks right, whose success is measured in zero sales, as the four-hundred-dollar bottle on the wine list exists to make the ninety-dollar bottle the sensible choice and the largest popcorn exists to sell the middle one; the carrier is the menu, and the clearing story calls an unsold item a mispricing when it is the one item doing its job. Adjacent to first-mover-forecloses' anchoring of a price expectation, which is about who sets the scale first; this is about a price that works by being declined.

Rack rate: a list price nobody pays, kept so that every real price can be a discount from it, granted selectively and felt as a favor, and so that a third party can be billed against it, as the hotel's posted rate and the hospital chargemaster that only the uninsured and the insurer's formula ever meet; the carrier is the discount, the price is for the very good on sale yet clears nothing for anyone, and removing it does not lower prices but removes the seller's power to give.

Quote that cannot be compared: a price built in a unit, bundle, or bespoke form no rival quotes in, so the buyer cannot perform the comparison a market needs, as the mobile plan whose every term differs from every other plan's, the hospital's bundled bill, and 'price on application'; the carrier is the form of the quote, it reverses the tier since it dissolves the class the tier made, and the clearing story assumes a market that this price was built to prevent. The reverse rule, mandatory unit pricing on the shelf, makes a market by an order about the price's form rather than its level.

residue.item: Bride price: a payment that constitutes an alliance between families rather than a purchase.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: possibly a distinct mechanism, a price that makes a relation, mirroring the invoice that ends one; but as written it is Peppercorn at the scale of kin (a payment that moves a union into the register the community can see) and needs a mechanism distinct from witnessing before admission.

residue.item: Scoreboard price: a share price or index that exists to be steered by, so the company manages the number rather than the firm.
residue.why: Rejected: carried by leverage-discoveries' index (the measure the system steers by, lighter to move than the system); the price adds nothing to that mechanism beyond being the index.

residue.item: Tribute: a recurring price for a continuing absence of harm, recurring because a single payment cannot be checked against an absence.
residue.why: Rejected: the recurrence is an enforcement schedule for a good exchange-ontologies lists as Protection; the price clears that market and does no second job.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real price usually does several of these at once (a rack rate is also a price for the stranger's eyes; a deposit also rations attention), and the list makes no claim to cover every job a price can hold.

The seriation is an itinerary by how much of the work the number itself does, not a ranking of importance, frequency, or profit; map edges are conditional authored claims, and the loop through the late fee is one reading of one industry's history.

The illustrative cases (the daycare fine, the video-store late fee, the chargemaster, the peppercorn rent, the gallery buying back its own artist, the prison phone contract) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories; the field evidence behind Invoice that ends the favor and Price as testimony is contested.

Prices that clear across time or across segments (surge pricing, early-bird tickets, a discount behind an identity fence) are deliberately outside: they are clearing with the date or the wall moved, and the number does its ordinary work.
Zero-price goods and gift economies are outside except where a nominal price crosses the line in or out (Peppercorn, Invoice that ends the favor, Mates' rates).

neighbors.left: Deposit that comes back: a price returned if the buyer does what they said, so it rations requests by putting money at risk rather than by collecting it, as the restaurant deposit refunded on arrival, earnest money on a house, and bail; the carrier is escrow, the net price is zero for everyone who keeps their word, and the clearing story cannot see a price that changes hands twice and ends where it began. It also earns the seller float, which is the one number in it a spreadsheet will find.
neighbors.right: Fee that holds the door: a price the seller hopes never to collect, as the cancellation fee, the late fee, and the liquidated-damages clause, which work by being believed and stop working when they are paid often, since a fee collected often enough to be optimized as revenue becomes a rack rate for lateness and the door it held swings open; the carrier is the threat, nothing changes hands on the good path where the deposit changes hands twice, and the clearing story sees a fee that is never paid as a price with no demand.
neighbors.separating_case: A wedding venue that takes a five-thousand-dollar deposit refunded on the day, against one that writes a five-thousand-dollar cancellation fee: on the good path the deposit changes hands twice and the fee never once; the deposit rations intent from the moment it is paid and earns the venue float whether or not the couple shows, while the fee rations nothing until it is believed and earns nothing until someone cancels. The case that separates them is the venue's own wish: it wants the deposit back in the couple's hands, and it wants the fee never to leave theirs.

checks.boundary_case: A discount behind an identity fence (the student price checked at the door, the drug priced by country with reimport banned) is out: it looks as if the price is doing extra work, but each segment clears at its own number and the wall, not the price, is the instrument. Rack rate is in on exactly that contrast, since nobody in any segment pays it.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Fee that holds the door → Invoice that ends the favor → Fee that holds the door, where a fee collected often enough to be optimized becomes the open price of an option, the old restraint does not return when the fee is dropped, and the seller must build a new threat one register lower. It shows an incompatibility between seriation neighbors, Velvet rope → Price as testimony, where a price that succeeds as testimony recruits the crowd the rope existed to thin. It shows two passages between levels, Six-minute increment → Tier that makes the kind, where a meter's instruction to individual buyers becomes a category in the market's vocabulary, and Go-away price → Velvet rope, where one-by-one refusals published become a screen on a class. And it shows two dependencies, Price that names the wrong payer → Price that goes to sleep, where a price with no payer at the user has no bill to wake, and Rack rate → Price for the stranger's eyes, where an unpaid list price poisons the record that third parties read.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a distinct thing the price does, a carrier, and a distinct miss in the clearing story; the strange members (a price whose success is zero sales, a price that changes hands twice and nets to nothing, a price that works by being nonzero, a price addressed to someone not in the trade) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into pricing advice.

next_crossfield_opening: Prices that are witnesses: connect Peppercorn and Price for the stranger's eyes with witness-architectures' Ledger that makes the debt and Arm's-length custody; ask which transactions exist only because a number was written down where a third party can read it, and whether a price can be a witness for the parties without also becoming a precedent for strangers.

gaps: The loop Fee that holds the door → Invoice that ends the favor → Fee that holds the door was illustrated by its own exit: the video store's abolished late fees became a subscription, which is the map's Price that goes to sleep, not a new door fee. Repaired by naming the fork on the edge (back to a lower door, as the library that bills replacement cost after thirty days, or out to a sleeping price) rather than dropping the loop. Under it: the seriation axis 'how much of the work the number itself does' was false for the last four stations (deposit and door fee work by size, decoy and rack rate by being high), so the far end is 'never collected', a second principle; renamed to which feature carries the work, no station moved. And Price that names the wrong payer bundled a different payer, a hidden payee, and the same buyer billed later; its own edge to Price that goes to sleep exposed it, since the overdrafter does not sleep.
accepted: Price that names the wrong payer: the price the buyer sees is set to produce a payment somewhere else, and that other payment, not the visible one, is what the seller designs for, so the buyer cannot see whose interest the seller serves, as the free checking account built to produce overdraft fees, the free search paid by the advertiser who is the actual customer, and the prison phone call priced high because the jailer who awarded the contract takes a commission from every minute; the carrier is the bundle or the tie, it is not a price merely collected later, since a net-thirty invoice is still the price the seller designs for, and the clearing story reads each price alone when the pair is the instrument.

Peppercorn: the existence of any price at all, however small, moves a transfer into the register a court can see, as the peppercorn rent makes a lease enforceable and the one-dollar sale gives a gift a buyer, a date, and a warranty to sue on; the carrier is the contract, the magnitude is irrelevant to a witness that reads only whether a price exists and useless against one that reads how much, since the tax office and the assessor look through a dollar sale to the gift beneath it, and the clearing story has no place for a price whose entire work is done by being nonzero.

Decoy that must not sell: an item priced so that its neighbor looks right, whose job is done by being declined and needs no sale, as the four-hundred-dollar bottle on the wine list exists to make the ninety-dollar bottle the sensible choice and the largest popcorn exists to sell the middle one; the carrier is the menu, the unpaid number belongs to a neighboring good rather than to the good it sells, and the clearing story calls an unsold item a mispricing when it is the one item doing its job. Adjacent to first-mover-forecloses' anchoring of a price expectation, which is about who sets the scale first; this is about a price that works by being declined.

residue.item: Velvet rope's nine-dollar coworking coffee case
residue.why: Critic kept the item and flagged the coffee as its weakest case, close to the congestion charge breath two rejected as clearing on a corrected cost, with the private bank's minimum balance as the true rope; no swap was required, so the text is unchanged and the swap is left to cultivation.

residue.item: Gate neighbors (Deposit that comes back / Fee that holds the door)
residue.why: Left as authored; the critic ran an additional neighbor test on Decoy that must not sell / Rack rate (separating case: the hospital MRI, chargemaster three thousand, negotiated six hundred, the uninsured billed the full number) and wrote its result into the Decoy repair rather than replacing the author's pair.

limits: Edge relabeled: Invoice that ends the favor → Fee that holds the door now names the loop's exit to a sleeping price and gives a case that loops (fines abolished, replacement cost billed after thirty days); form_inference now states the loop as also a fork. Seriation axis renamed from how much work the number does to which feature of the price carries it; order, endpoints, hinge, and consequential adjacency unchanged. Boundary claim now lists the third-class carriage among simplified histories (the 1844 statute fixed fare and accommodation together). No items cut; nothing preserved against the critic, since no repair domesticated a strange mechanism. Not applied as a limit: the critic's price-match-guarantee boundary case and the posted-fuel-price coordination signal are recorded here as an opening, not added as an item.
seed: The map already contains a contradiction it has not noticed, and it is the best thing in it: Mates' rates says the guest-friend's token payment 'says this is not a purchase', and Peppercorn says the one-dollar sale 'makes a gift into a purchase'. The same nominal number is read oppositely by two witnesses at once, the friends and the court, and the tax office reads it a third way. So a price is not addressed to a market but to a set of readers who disagree about what it means, and the operator's question becomes: which witness am I pricing for, and what does the number say to the ones I am not? That fork (one number, several registers, each reading a different feature: existence, magnitude, or the fact of haggling) would also resolve the ledger's bride-price residue, which is a payment that constitutes an alliance to kin, a purchase to a court, and nothing at all to a market; it connects directly to witness-architectures and is a list, not a repair to this map.
